sanskrit: tad etat saṃpradṛśyaiva karmabhūmiṃ praviśya tām śubhāny ācaritavyāni paralokam abhīpsatā
english: Seeing all this clearly, one who longs for the world beyond should enter this realm of action and there perform what is holy and good.

sanskrit: māsartusaṃjñāparivartakena; sūryāgninā rātridivendhanena svakarmaniṣṭhāphalasākṣikeṇa; bhūtāni kālaḥ pacati prasahya
english: By the fire of the sun, which turns the round of months and seasons, fed with the fuel of night and day, witness to the fruit that follows upon each being's own works, Time ripens all creatures by main force.

sanskrit: dhanena kiṃ yan na dadāti nāśnute; balena kiṃ yena ripūn na bādhate śrutena kiṃ yena na dharmam ācaret; kim ātmanā yo na jitendriyo vaśī
english: What is the use of wealth from which one neither gives nor enjoys? Of strength by which one does not subdue one's foes? Of learning by which one does not practice the dharma? Of a self that has not mastered and made obedient the senses?

sanskrit: idaṃ dvaipāyanavaco hitam uktaṃ niśamya tu śuko gataḥ parityajya pitaraṃ mokṣadeśikam
english: Having heard this wholesome counsel spoken by Dvaipāyana, Śuka departed, leaving behind his father, the teacher of liberation.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ vyāsasya dharmātmā śuko jajñe mahātapāḥ siddhiṃ ca paramāṃ prāptas tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How was Śuka, righteous of soul and of great austerity, born to Vyāsa, and how did he attain the supreme perfection? Tell me this, grandsire.

sanskrit: kasyāṃ cotpādayām āsa śukaṃ vyāsas tapodhanaḥ na hy asya jananīṃ vidma janma cāgryaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: And upon whom did Vyāsa, rich in austerity, beget Śuka? For we do not know the mother of that great soul, nor his surpassing birth.

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca bālasya sataḥ sūkṣmajñāne gatā matiḥ yathā nānyasya loke 'smin dvitīyasyeha kasya cit
english: And how, while still a child, did his mind reach into subtle knowledge, such as the mind of no other, no second, in this whole world has done?

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ vistareṇa mahādyute na hi me tṛptir astīha śṛṇvato 'mṛtam uttamam
english: This I wish to hear at length, O most radiant one, for there is no satiety for me here as I listen to this supreme nectar.

sanskrit: māhātmyam ātmayogaṃ ca vijñānaṃ ca śukasya ha yathāvad ānupūrvyeṇa tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Tell me, grandsire, faithfully and in due order, the greatness of Śuka, his union with the Self, and his deep wisdom.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca na hāyanair na palitair na vittena na bandhubhiḥ ṛṣayaś cakrire dharmaṃ yo 'nūcānaḥ sa no mahān
english: Bhīṣma said: Not by years, not by grey hairs, not by wealth, not by kinsmen did the sages measure dharma: he who is learned in the Veda, he is great among us.

sanskrit: tapomūlam idaṃ sarvaṃ yan māṃ pṛcchasi pāṇḍava tad indriyāṇi saṃyamya tapo bhavati nānyathā
english: All this about which you ask me, son of Pāṇḍu, has austerity for its root; and only by restraining the senses does austerity arise, and in no other way.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ prasaṅgena doṣam ṛcchaty asaṃśayam saṃniyamya tu tāny eva siddhiṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: By attachment to the senses a man surely meets with ruin; but by subduing those very senses he attains perfection.

sanskrit: aśvamedhasahasrasya vājapeyaśatasya ca yogasya kalayā tāta na tulyaṃ vidyate phalam
english: The fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices and of a hundred Vājapeyas, my son, is found not to equal even a fraction of yoga's reward.

sanskrit: atra te vartayiṣyāmi janmayogaphalaṃ yathā śukasyāgryāṃ gatiṃ caiva durvidām akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: On this I shall relate to you the fruit of Śuka's birth and of his yoga, and that supreme course of his, hard to be known by the unperfected.

sanskrit: meruśṛṅge kila purā karṇikāravanāyute vijahāra mahādevo bhīmair bhūtagaṇair vṛtaḥ
english: Of old, they say, upon the peak of Meru, thick with groves of karṇikāra trees, the Great God roamed, surrounded by his terrible hosts of spirits.

sanskrit: śailarājasutā caiva devī tatrābhavat purā tatra divyaṃ tapas tepe kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ
english: There too of old was the goddess, daughter of the king of mountains; and there the lord Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana performed his divine austerity.

sanskrit: yogenātmānam āviśya yogadharmaparāyaṇaḥ dhārayan sa tapas tepe putrārthaṃ kurusattama
english: Entering into his own self through yoga, wholly devoted to the discipline of yoga, holding fast, he wrought austerity for the sake of a son, O best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: agner bhūmer apāṃ vāyor antarikṣasya cābhibho vīryeṇa saṃmitaḥ putro mama bhūyād iti sma ha
english: "May a son be born to me, O mighty one, equal in power to fire, to earth, to water, to wind, and to the firmament" — so he prayed.

sanskrit: saṃkalpenātha so 'nena duṣprāpeṇākṛtātmabhiḥ varayām āsa deveśam āsthitas tapa uttamam
english: With this resolve, hard to be reached by the unperfected, established in the highest austerity, he sought a boon of the Lord of the gods.

sanskrit: atiṣṭhan mārutāhāraḥ śataṃ kila samāḥ prabhuḥ ārādhayan mahādevaṃ bahurūpam umāpatim
english: Feeding only on air, the lord stood firm, they say, for a hundred years, worshipping the Great God of many forms, the consort of Umā.

sanskrit: tatra brahmarṣayaś caiva sarve devarṣayas tathā lokapālāś ca lokeśaṃ sādhyāś ca vasubhiḥ saha
english: There gathered all the brahmin-sages and the divine sages too, the guardians of the worlds before the Lord of the worlds, and the Sādhyas together with the Vasus.

sanskrit: ādityāś caiva rudrāś ca divākaraniśākarau maruto mārutaś caiva sāgarāḥ saritas tathā
english: The Ādityas and the Rudras, the maker of day and the maker of night, the Maruts and the Wind, the oceans and the rivers as well.

sanskrit: aśvinau devagandharvās tathā nāradaparvatau viśvāvasuś ca gandharvaḥ siddhāś cāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ
english: The two Aśvins, the celestial gandharvas, and the pair Nārada and Parvata, Viśvāvasu the gandharva, the Siddhas, and the hosts of apsarases.

sanskrit: tatra rudro mahādevaḥ karṇikāramayīṃ śubhām dhārayāṇaḥ srajaṃ bhāti jyotsnām iva niśākaraḥ
english: There Rudra, the Great God, wearing a fair garland wrought of karṇikāra blossoms, shone like the moon clothed in its moonlight.

sanskrit: tasmin divye vane ramye devadevarṣisaṃkule āsthitaḥ paramaṃ yogam ṛṣiḥ putrārtham udyataḥ
english: In that lovely divine forest, thronged with gods and divine sages, the seer, established in the supreme yoga, stood intent upon his desire for a son.

sanskrit: na cāsya hīyate varṇo na glānir upajāyate trayāṇām api lokānāṃ tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: His radiance did not fade, nor did any weariness arise in him; and to all three worlds this seemed a wonder.

sanskrit: jaṭāś ca tejasā tasya vaiśvānaraśikhopamāḥ prajvalantyaḥ sma dṛśyante yuktasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: And the matted locks of that yoked one of measureless splendor were seen ablaze with his fiery power, like tongues of the all-consuming fire.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeyo hi bhagavān etad ākhyātavān mama sa devacaritānīha kathayām āsa me sadā
english: For the blessed Mārkaṇḍeya it was who told me this; he it was who ever recounted to me the deeds of the gods.

sanskrit: tā etādyāpi kṛṣṇasya tapasā tena dīpitāḥ agnivarṇā jaṭās tāta prakāśante mahātmanaḥ
english: Even to this day, my son, those matted locks of the great-souled Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, kindled by that austerity and fire-hued, shine forth.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhena tapasā tasya bhaktyā ca bhārata maheśvaraḥ prasannātmā cakāra manasā matim
english: By austerity of such a kind and by his devotion, O Bhārata, the Great Lord, his heart made gracious, formed a resolve within his mind.

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ bhagavāṃs tryambakaḥ prahasann iva evaṃvidhas te tanayo dvaipāyana bhaviṣyati
english: And the blessed three-eyed god spoke to him, as though smiling: "A son of just such a kind shall be yours, O Dvaipāyana."

sanskrit: yathā hy agnir yathā vāyur yathā bhūmir yathā jalam yathā ca khaṃ tathā śuddho bhaviṣyati suto mahān
english: "Pure as fire, pure as wind, pure as earth, pure as water, and pure as space — so shall your great son be."

sanskrit: tadbhāvabhāvī tadbuddhis tadātmā tadapāśrayaḥ tejasāvṛtya lokāṃs trīn yaśaḥ prāpsyati kevalam
english: "Sharing that nature, that understanding, that very self, taking refuge in that alone, enveloping the three worlds with his splendor, he shall win unrivalled glory."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sa labdhvā paramaṃ devād varaṃ satyavatīsutaḥ araṇīṃ tv atha saṃgṛhya mamanthāgnicikīrṣayā
english: Bhīṣma said: Having won this supreme boon from the god, the son of Satyavatī took up the fire-drilling wood and churned it, wishing to kindle the sacred fire.

sanskrit: atha rūpaṃ paraṃ rājan bibhratīṃ svena tejasā ghṛtācīṃ nāmāpsarasam apaśyad bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: Then, O king, the blessed seer beheld an apsaras named Ghṛtācī, bearing a surpassing beauty radiant with her own glow.

sanskrit: ṛṣir apsarasaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasā kāmamohitaḥ abhavad bhagavān vyāso vane tasmin yudhiṣṭhira
english: Beholding the apsaras, the blessed seer Vyāsa was on the instant overpowered by desire there in that forest, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: sā ca kṛtvā tadā vyāsaṃ kāmasaṃvignamānasam śukī bhūtvā mahārāja ghṛtācī samupāgamat
english: And she, having made Vyāsa's mind tremble with longing, then became a parrot-hen, O great king, and so Ghṛtācī drew near.

sanskrit: sa tām apsarasaṃ dṛṣṭvā rūpeṇānyena saṃvṛtām śarīrajenānugataḥ sarvagātrātigena ha
english: Seeing that apsaras cloaked in another form, he was followed close by the body-born god of love that surged through all his limbs.

sanskrit: sa tu dhairyeṇa mahatā nigṛhṇan hṛcchayaṃ muniḥ na śaśāka niyantuṃ tad vyāsaḥ pravisṛtaṃ manaḥ bhāvitvāc caiva bhāvasya ghṛtācyā vapuṣā hṛtaḥ
english: Though with great firmness the sage strove to hold down the desire lodged in his heart, Vyāsa could not restrain his mind once it had streamed forth; for, the passion being destined to be, he was carried away by the form of Ghṛtācī.

sanskrit: yatnān niyacchatas tasya muner agnicikīrṣayā araṇyām eva sahasā tasya śukram avāpatat
english: As the sage labored to restrain himself in his wish to kindle the fire, his seed fell suddenly upon the very drilling-wood.

sanskrit: so 'viśaṅkena manasā tathaiva dvijasattamaḥ araṇīṃ mamantha brahmarṣis tasyāṃ jajñe śuko nṛpa
english: With a mind untroubled, that best of the twice-born, the brahmin-sage, churned the drilling-wood even so; and therein was Śuka born, O king.

sanskrit: śukre nirmathyamāne tu śuko jajñe mahātapāḥ paramarṣir mahāyogī araṇīgarbhasaṃbhavaḥ
english: As the seed was being churned forth, Śuka was born, of great austerity, a supreme seer, a mighty yogin, sprung from the womb of the drilling-wood.

sanskrit: yathādhvare samiddho 'gnir bhāti havyam upāttavān tathārūpaḥ śuko jajñe prajvalann iva tejasā
english: As the kindled fire at the sacrifice shines forth when it has received the oblation, so was Śuka born in that very likeness, blazing as it were with splendor.

sanskrit: bibhrat pituś ca kauravya rūpavarṇam anuttamam babhau tadā bhāvitātmā vidhūmo 'gnir iva jvalan
english: Bearing his father's matchless form and hue, O Kaurava, that perfected soul then shone like a smokeless flame ablaze.

sanskrit: taṃ gaṅgā saritāṃ śreṣṭhā merupṛṣṭhe janeśvara svarūpiṇī tadābhyetya snāpayām āsa vāriṇā
english: Then Gaṅgā, the best of rivers, taking her own embodied shape, came to him on Meru's height, O lord of men, and bathed him in her waters.

sanskrit: antarikṣāc ca kauravya daṇḍaḥ kṛṣṇājinaṃ ca ha papāta bhuvi rājendra śukasyārthe mahātmanaḥ
english: And from the sky, O Kaurava, a staff and a black antelope-skin fell to earth, O sovereign of kings, for the sake of the great-souled Śuka.

sanskrit: jegīyante sma gandharvā nanṛtuś cāpsarogaṇāḥ devadundubhayaś caiva prāvādyanta mahāsvanāḥ
english: The gandharvas sang again and again, the hosts of apsarases danced, and the kettledrums of the gods sounded forth with mighty peals.

sanskrit: viśvāvasuś ca gandharvas tathā tumburunāradau hāhāhūhū ca gandharvau tuṣṭuvuḥ śukasaṃbhavam
english: And Viśvāvasu the gandharva, and Tumburu and Nārada, and the gandharvas Hāhā and Hūhū extolled the birth of Śuka.

sanskrit: tatra śakrapurogāś ca lokapālāḥ samāgatāḥ devā devarṣayaś caiva tathā brahmarṣayo 'pi ca
english: There assembled the guardians of the worlds, with Śakra at their head, the gods and the divine sages, and the brahmin-sages too.

sanskrit: divyāni sarvapuṣpāṇi pravavarṣātra mārutaḥ jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ caiva prahṛṣṭam abhavaj jagat
english: The Wind rained down there every kind of celestial flower, and the whole world, moving and unmoving, was filled with joy.

sanskrit: taṃ mahātmā svayaṃ prītyā devyā saha mahādyutiḥ jātamātraṃ muneḥ putraṃ vidhinopānayat tadā
english: The great-souled god of mighty splendor, together with the goddess, then with affection himself performed in due rite the investiture of the sage's son, scarcely born.

sanskrit: tasya deveśvaraḥ śakro divyam adbhutadarśanam dadau kamaṇḍaluṃ prītyā devavāsāṃsi cābhibho
english: To him Śakra, lord of the gods, gave with affection a water-pot of marvellous, divine appearance, and celestial garments, O mighty one.

sanskrit: haṃsāś ca śatapatrāś ca sārasāś ca sahasraśaḥ pradakṣiṇam avartanta śukāś cāṣāś ca bhārata
english: Geese and hundred-petalled cranes and sārasa birds by the thousand, and parrots and blue jays, O Bhārata, circled him in reverence.

sanskrit: āraṇeyas tathā divyaṃ prāpya janma mahādyutiḥ tatraivovāsa medhāvī vratacārī samāhitaḥ
english: Thus the son of the drilling-wood, of great splendor, having gained his divine birth, dwelt there, wise, a keeper of vows, and inwardly composed.

sanskrit: utpannamātraṃ taṃ vedāḥ sarahasyāḥ sasaṃgrahāḥ upatasthur mahārāja yathāsya pitaraṃ tathā
english: No sooner was he born than the Vedas, with their mysteries and their compendia, came and waited upon him, O great king, even as they had upon his father.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatiṃ tu vavre sa vedavedāṅgabhāṣyavit upādhyāyaṃ mahārāja dharmam evānucintayan
english: Knower of the Vedas, their auxiliaries, and their commentaries, he chose Bṛhaspati for his teacher, O great king, meditating ever upon dharma alone.

sanskrit: so 'dhītya vedān akhilān sarahasyān sasaṃgrahān itihāsaṃ ca kārtsnyena rājaśāstrāṇi cābhibho
english: Having studied all the Vedas with their mysteries and compendia, and the ancient lore in its entirety, and the sciences of statecraft, O mighty one,

sanskrit: gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā samāvṛtto mahāmuniḥ ugraṃ tapaḥ samārebhe brahmacārī samāhitaḥ
english: the great sage gave his teacher the closing fee, returned home, and, a chaste student inwardly composed, undertook a fierce austerity.

sanskrit: devatānām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca bālye 'pi sa mahātapāḥ saṃmantraṇīyo mānyaś ca jñānena tapasā tathā
english: Even in childhood, that one of great austerity was fit to be consulted by gods and seers, and honored by them for his knowledge and his penance.

sanskrit: na tv asya ramate buddhir āśrameṣu narādhipa triṣu gārhasthyamūleṣu mokṣadharmānudarśinaḥ
english: Yet his mind, O lord of men, looking ever toward the discipline of liberation, took no delight in the three orders of life that have the householder's state for their root.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sa mokṣam anucintyaiva śukaḥ pitaram abhyagāt prāhābhivādya ca guruṃ śreyorthī vinayānvitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Brooding upon liberation alone, Śuka went to his father, and, seeking the highest good, full of humility, he saluted his teacher and spoke:

sanskrit: mokṣadharmeṣu kuśalo bhagavān prabravītu me yathā me manasaḥ śāntiḥ paramā saṃbhavet prabho
english: "You, blessed one, are skilled in the laws of liberation: instruct me, lord, in such a way that the supreme peace of mind may arise in me."

sanskrit: śrutvā putrasya vacanaṃ paramarṣir uvāca tam adhīṣva putra mokṣaṃ vai dharmāṃś ca vividhān api
english: Hearing his son's words, the supreme seer said to him: "Study, my son, both liberation and the manifold dharmas as well."

sanskrit: pitur niyogāj jagrāha śuko brahmavidāṃ varaḥ yogaśāstraṃ ca nikhilaṃ kāpilaṃ caiva bhārata
english: At his father's bidding Śuka, best of those who know the Brahman, mastered the whole science of yoga and also the Kāpila teaching, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa taṃ brāhmyā śriyā yuktaṃ brahmatulyaparākramam mene putraṃ yadā vyāso mokṣavidyāviśāradam
english: When Vyāsa saw his son endowed with the splendor of the Brahman, his prowess equal to Brahmā's, and accomplished in the lore of liberation,

sanskrit: uvāca gaccheti tadā janakaṃ mithileśvaram sa te vakṣyati mokṣārthaṃ nikhilena viśeṣataḥ
english: he said: "Go now to Janaka, the lord of Mithilā; he will expound to you the whole matter of liberation, fully and in detail."

sanskrit: pitur niyogād agaman maithilaṃ janakaṃ nṛpam praṣṭuṃ dharmasya niṣṭhāṃ vai mokṣasya ca parāyaṇam
english: At his father's bidding he set out toward Janaka, king of Mithilā, to ask of him the consummation of dharma and the highest goal of liberation.

sanskrit: uktaś ca mānuṣeṇa tvaṃ pathā gacchety avismitaḥ na prabhāveṇa gantavyam antarikṣacareṇa vai
english: And he was told, unsurprised: "You are to go by a human road; you must not travel by your power, coursing through the sky."

sanskrit: ārjaveṇaiva gantavyaṃ na sukhānveṣiṇā pathā nānveṣṭavyā viśeṣās tu viśeṣā hi prasaṅginaḥ
english: "You must go by the straight way, not by a path that seeks comfort; nor must distinctions be sought after, for distinctions breed attachment."

sanskrit: ahaṃkāro na kartavyo yājye tasmin narādhipe sthātavyaṃ ca vaśe tasya sa te chetsyati saṃśayam
english: "No pride is to be shown before that king for whom we serve as priests; you must remain subject to him, and he will cut away your doubt."

sanskrit: sa dharmakuśalo rājā mokṣaśāstraviśāradaḥ yājyo mama sa yad brūyāt tat kāryam aviśaṅkayā
english: "That king is skilled in dharma and accomplished in the science of liberation; he is one for whom I officiate, and whatever he says is to be done without misgiving."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa dharmātmā jagāma mithilāṃ muniḥ padbhyāṃ śakto 'ntarikṣeṇa krāntuṃ bhūmiṃ sasāgarām
english: Thus addressed, that righteous sage went on foot to Mithilā, though he was able to traverse the sea-girt earth through the air.

sanskrit: sa girīṃś cāpy atikramya nadīs tīrtvā sarāṃsi ca bahuvyālamṛgākīrṇā vividhāś cāṭavīs tathā
english: Crossing over mountains, fording rivers and lakes, and the manifold forests thronged with many serpents and beasts of prey,

sanskrit: meror hareś ca dve varṣe varṣaṃ haimavataṃ tathā krameṇaiva vyatikramya bhārataṃ varṣam āsadat
english: passing in turn beyond the two regions of Meru and Hari and the region of Himavat, he reached the land of Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa deśān vividhān paśyaṃś cīnahūṇaniṣevitān āryāvartam imaṃ deśam ājagāma mahāmuniḥ
english: Beholding various lands inhabited by the Cīnas and the Hūṇas, the great sage came at last to this land of Āryāvarta.

sanskrit: pitur vacanam ājñāya tam evārthaṃ vicintayan adhvānaṃ so 'ticakrāma khe 'caraḥ khe carann iva
english: Mindful of his father's word and pondering that very purpose, he passed along the road, a sky-farer faring as it were through the sky.

sanskrit: pattanāni ca ramyāṇi sphītāni nagarāṇi ca ratnāni ca vicitrāṇi śukaḥ paśyan na paśyati
english: Lovely market-towns and prosperous cities and jewels of varied kinds — Śuka, though he saw them, saw them not.

sanskrit: udyānāni ca ramyāṇi tathaivāyatanāni ca puṇyāni caiva tīrthāni so 'tikramya tathādhvanaḥ
english: Lovely gardens, and temples, and holy fording-places too he passed by upon his road,

sanskrit: so 'cireṇaiva kālena videhān āsasāda ha rakṣitān dharmarājena janakena mahātmanā
english: and in no long while he came to the land of the Videhas, guarded by the great-souled Janaka, that righteous king.

sanskrit: tatra grāmān bahūn paśyan bahvannarasabhojanān pallīghoṣān samṛddhāṃś ca bahugokulasaṃkulān
english: There he saw many villages where food and savory fare abounded, and thriving hamlets and herdsmen's settlements teeming with many a cattle-fold.
